trajectory_summary: This call is procedurally solid — legitimacy holds, the bill gets collected efficiently via text, an appointment is locked with a specific day and time, and the rep avoids getting drawn into technical debates about shading and production. But it leaves real value on the table: a fully articulated off-grid/generator-backup intent is never flagged as a possible scenario mismatch, a competitor's shortfall data point is never probed, and a disclosed psychiatric/anxiety detail gets a bare acknowledgment. The call ends warm and booked, but the closer is walking in without key context flagged.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow, the 5th) and time (3PM) are agreed by both parties, with the rep confirming 'Sweet. So we'll find tomorrow, 3PM.' The visit appears to be an in-person design walkthrough ('bring the design out to you') rather than a phone call. No co-owner (wife Laura) was explicitly confirmed for the appointment despite being mentioned.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: My last bill is right around $4.50. Average is closer to $2.50.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures the bill figure and later gets the actual photo via text, but never verbally reflects the number back as the customer's reason to act — the closest she gets is a generic 'cover as much of your bill as you can' at 13:44, which doesn't tie back to the specific figure the customer gave. The flip should have landed right after 'Perfect' at 02:47, turning the $250 average into an explicit motivator tied to his stated goal of not relying on Dominion at all.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: I honestly, I just I would rather be off grid completely.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asks the interest question and the customer gives a detailed, unusual reason (full energy independence, not just bill savings), but the rep never reinforces this specific motivation when setting or buttoning up the appointment — the close is generic ('cover as much of your bill as you can') rather than tied to his stated off-grid independence goal.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Non-standard scenario flagged but never escalated
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I honestly, I just I would rather be off grid completely.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer states three separate times that he wants full off-grid disconnection with generator backup — a fundamentally different scenario than a standard grid-tied solar sale. This should be explicitly flagged in the handoff so the closer knows to address feasibility head-on, rather than discovering it live.

key_moments.quote: I honestly, I just I would rather be off grid completely.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer is describing a fully off-grid intent (no utility connection at all, generator backup, battery, possible rainwater collection) which is a different product scenario than a standard grid-tied solar install. Ion's documented catalog doesn't clearly address off-grid systems, so it's unclear whether this is even a serviceable request — that judgment call is closer-tier, but the setter had an opportunity to flag the ambiguity rather than silently log it.

key_moments.quote: I do do I do just happen to have my most recent bill because you're not the only company I've been talking to, and the only way I could get it to them was to take a picture of it and send it to them via text message.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer explicitly discloses he's shopping multiple companies and has already sent his bill to at least one competitor, then later reveals a 65%-production shortfall from one of them. The rep never asks which company(ies) or what they proposed.

key_moments.quote: the problem they're having is they've only got 36 feet to run to work with.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the second touch on the competing-quote thread — the customer is now giving specific technical detail (run length, shading, winter solstice sun angle) about a competitor's proposed design. The rep listens and says 'Okay' without asking who provided this design or probing further.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. My my team will we'll definitely explore all the options, see what we can do to get you, you know, as much production as possible, cover as much of your bill as you can.
key_moments.stewart_read: Faced with a detailed technical objection about shading and winter-solstice sun angles, the rep correctly does not engage in a technical debate and instead bridges to the design team — a textbook universal_escape_hatch deflection, not scope creep.
